h1: Christmas and Advent Decorating for Churches
heroIntro: Welcome visiting families the moment they pull into the parking lot. We design, install, maintain, and take down Advent and Christmas lighting around your weekly service schedule.
intro: Advent and Christmas Eve bring more visitors, more evening services, and more people walking up to your doors after dark than almost any other stretch of the church calendar. We install roofline lighting, entrance trees, wreaths, and pathway lighting for churches across South-Western Ontario and the western GTA, working around your weekly service calendar rather than the other way around. Our crews are fully insured and WSIB-compliant, and we bring the aerial lifts needed for a steeple or a tall sanctuary roofline that a volunteer or a facilities lead shouldn't be climbing to reach.

Because most churches make décor decisions through a board of trustees or a facilities committee working from a fixed annual budget, we build every proposal to fit that process rather than asking for a rushed decision in November. Design, installation, mid-season maintenance, and takedown after Epiphany are part of one quote, with optional storage so garland and lit trees don't need to live in a closet at the church the rest of the year. Booking opens in late summer, and we schedule around your Advent and Christmas Eve service calendar from the start.
whatWeInstall: Roofline lighting outlining the sanctuary and entrance facade
Lit trees at the main entrance and parking lot approach
Wreaths and bows on the sanctuary doors
Garland along the entrance ramp, railing, or staircase
A decorated tree for the narthex, foyer, or fellowship hall
Accent lighting for a steeple or bell tower where roof access allows
Pathway and parking lot lighting for evening Advent services
Timer-controlled displays that run through Christmas Eve and into January

whyItPays.heading: A warm welcome for visiting families
whyItPays.text: Advent and Christmas Eve draw people who don't attend regularly the rest of the year, including visiting family and newcomers deciding whether to come back in January. A well-lit parking lot, entrance, and pathway make that first impression easier before anyone even reaches the sanctuary doors, and it reflects the same warmth a congregation hopes to offer inside. It's a small, visible way of extending hospitality before a single word is spoken.

whyItPays.heading: No volunteer on a ladder over the roofline
whyItPays.text: Every church has someone willing to climb up and string lights along the roof or the steeple, and every church would be better off if that person didn't have to. Our crews are fully insured and WSIB-compliant, and we bring aerial lifts sized for a sanctuary roofline or bell tower, working around weekday office hours and your service calendar so nothing interferes with choir practice, youth group, or a midweek Advent gathering.

whyItPays.heading: One predictable cost for the trustees to approve
whyItPays.text: Church budgets are set well in advance and usually reviewed by a board or trustees before anything is spent, so a holiday lighting quote that changes every year makes that harder to plan around. A multi-year program bundles design, installation, mid-season maintenance, and January or Epiphany takedown into one invoice, with storage available so the church doesn't need closet space for garland and lit trees the other eleven months of the year.

process: Site visit or photos with your facilities lead or trustees
Design proposal built around your Advent and Christmas Eve service calendar
Installation scheduled around weekday office hours and evening services
Mid-season maintenance and takedown after Epiphany, with optional storage

faq.q: Can installation happen around our weekly services and events?
faq.a: Yes. We schedule around your regular service times, midweek gatherings, and any Advent events you already have booked, and most sanctuary exteriors and entrances are finished in a single weekday visit. If your church has a specific quiet window, like weekday mornings before staff arrive, we'll plan around that rather than showing up during a service or rehearsal.

faq.q: How long does approval usually take through a board or trustees?
faq.a: That varies by congregation, but we provide a written proposal and quote early enough for a board to review it at a regular meeting rather than rushing a decision. Because booking fills by mid-November, we recommend starting the conversation with trustees in September if you want the display up well before Advent begins.

faq.q: Do the lights need to come down right after Christmas Day?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many churches keep lighting running through Epiphany in early January, since Advent and Christmas services often extend past December 25th. We schedule takedown after your season officially ends, whenever that is for your congregation, rather than forcing a fixed date, and safe roof access in January or February weather is factored into the plan.

faq.q: Is our volunteer team responsible for any part of the setup?
faq.a: No. Our fully insured, WSIB-compliant crew handles design, installation, maintenance, and takedown from start to finish, including anything at height like the steeple or sanctuary roofline. Your facilities lead is only involved for the initial site visit and to point out anything specific to your building, like an outdoor outlet location or an area to avoid.
